interpretation_limits: All 49 primary events have ordinary service-problem wording; four manually severe checkpoints are later repeated observations from two events. Three are literal severe-delay notices and one is a no-service/reroute notice.
The primary incident-profile result is four Switch recommendations, with one comparable meaningful gain and three unknowns. A one-of-one scorable gain is not a general success-rate estimate.

Across all 322 correlated checkpoints, incident-profile strict advice has 44 Switch recommendations: 15 comparable outcomes (11 gains and four practical ties), plus 29 unknowns. Repeated checkpoints are not independent trials.

All four comparable Grand Central model Switch gains are 5-to-4 substitutions between the same boarding and alighting stations. Six different-path Switch recommendations in that corridor have unknown outcomes.
The pilot primary positive is also selected by raw MTA and saves the same 1415 seconds; it does not establish improvement from the historical correction.

Court Square 05:51 ordinary-disruption illustration has 4970 seconds proxy savings for model-selected F versus fixed 7 Stay. Raw-MTA threshold advice stays, but raw-MTA fastest available route is E and is 27 seconds faster than the model F proxy; distinguish the threshold-policy effect from selecting the globally best route.

No literal severe-delay checkpoint contains a quantifiably successful Switch. The no-service/reroute checkpoint recommends same-path 4 over 5 but both endpoint outcomes are unavailable and both lines are named in the raw alert; this is not evidence of a safe or beneficial severe reroute.

Current Google route paths are fixed reference paths. Present-day Google minutes are not historical outcomes. All outcome durations are screened final-MTA proxies plus fixed walking assumptions, not independent passenger measurements.
